title: What was Camp X?
summary: Josh and Chuck cover Camp X, a secret World War Two training camp for saboteurs, agents, propagandists, and Morse code operators, located near Oshawa on Lake Ontario in Ontario, Canada. They explain its origins in British Security Coordination (a British intelligence office at Rockefeller Center in New York), the camp's training methods (live fire, instinctive shooting, close combat, and psychological pressure), notable figures such as William Stevenson, Bill Donovan, Gustav Biela, and Fairburn, the Hydra radio station that relayed transmissions to Bletchley Park, the camp's closing in 1945, and its later Cold War use for interrogating defector Igor Gouzenko. The episode closes with a listener mail segment from a champagne professional correcting earlier episode claims about champagne production and pricing.

segments.title: Tour announcement and intro
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck announce 2017 North America tour dates, introduce the episode as a Ed Grabowski article, and mention a listener suggestion for Camp X.

segments.title: What Camp X was and World War Two context
segments.summary: Camp X is introduced as a secret World War Two training camp for saboteurs, propagandists, Morse code operators, and assassins. The hosts discuss US isolationism before Pearl Harbor and British intelligence efforts to influence American opinion, with Roald Dahl and Ian Fleming's involvement.

segments.title: Origins: British Security Coordination and site selection
segments.summary: British Security Coordination set up an office at Rockefeller Center in New York, led by William Stevenson. The camp was set up in Canada because the US was neutral, and the site near Oshawa, Ontario was bought under a front company. The Prime Minister was not told until it was underway. The camp had many names, including STS 103 and Project Hydra's codes.

segments.title: Camp X opening and naming
segments.summary: Camp X opened on December 6, 1941, the day before Pearl Harbor, after which the US entered the war. The hosts discuss the camp's various unofficial and official names and why the name Camp X came from locals.

segments.title: Training regimen at Camp X
segments.summary: Trainees learned map reading, bare-hand fighting, shooting in the dark, and instinctive gun fighting. Training included live fire, endurance tests, and fake sabotage such as staging a train theft and fake explosives. Andy Durovich's account is cited.

segments.title: Instructors and close combat methods
segments.summary: Commandant Bill Brooker is described as a disciplinarian open to unorthodox methods. Dan Fairburn taught close combat with a no-holds-barred approach. Bill Donovan is named the father of the CIA, and Gustav Biela, a French Canadian saboteur, is described as the camp's best student; he was executed by the Nazis.

segments.title: Hydra radio station and women's role
segments.summary: The Hydra radio station at Camp X, staffed partly by Canadian women, relayed encoded transmissions to Bletchley Park, including messages between Roosevelt and Churchill. Camp X closed in April 1945, and the Cold War interrogation of defector Igor Gouzenko took place there. The site was later bulldozed and a plaque commemorates William Stevenson.

segments.title: Listener mail: champagne corrections and outro
segments.summary: A listener who works in champagne corrects claims from an earlier episode, including grape pressing and riddling methods and bottle prices. Josh and Chuck close with social media and website information.
